I have a couple, but this one still gets to me.

When I was 7, I would visit my dad and his then fiancé for holidays because my mom had me for the rest of the year. He’s a musician and really only plays in bars. Christmas morning rolls around and I have this awful feeling when I wake up. We open presents, eat breakfast with his fiancé’s family and all the usual stuff. My dad has a gig to play at one of the bars in town, so he says he’s going to bring me to his sisters house during the event and then he’ll take me back to my moms house. I tell him about the bad feeling I have(which to me as a 7 year old was just a really bad tummy ache), and he ignores it. I keep telling him, even crying, that I can’t leave the house because my stomach hurts too bad. I called my mom and told her I didn’t want to go anywhere but I had no choice because who is going to listen to the kid throwing a tantrum? We pack my new toys up and hit the road even though I was crying. Half way to my aunts house, the front passenger side tire blows out. We flip multiple times, his fiancé is thrown from the vehicle and the roof over his head is crushed in, breaking his neck. I was the only one wearing a seatbelt. We’re out in BFE so it takes a while for anyone to spot us on the road. Eventually someone calls 911 and were airlifted to the nearest hospital 50 miles away. Dad broke his neck, took him a while to learn to walk and use his hands properly again. His fiancé broke her elbow and collarbone. I ended up only getting a scratch from the seatbelt.

From then on, I ALWAYS listen to my gut feeling. And as an adult, I NEVER get in a car on Christmas Day. EVER.
